derivation: difference of independent sample means has variance sigma^2*(1/|S| + 1/|S^c|) = sigma^2*N/(|S||S^c|); dividing by the standard error yields the scale-free factor sqrt(|S||S^c|/N)

correction_to_t0.note: The previous tick reported the whole-scene case as a pass under 'G2_whole_scene_support_collapses'. That label was wrong: the support mean equals the scene mean and the complement mean is zero, but the original evidence then equals <l, scene_mean>, a non-zero scene-level term. That is the degeneracy the probe was meant to catch, not a pass.

O3_tiny_mask_sensitivity_regression.interpretation: standardizing the contrast removes the spurious tiny-mask advantage, and it also removes genuine tiny-mask sensitivity; a 1-point support carries little evidence, so this is the honest cost of an unbiased null rather than a regression in the mechanism's useful range

O4_single_language_direction.note: with an affine or bilinear g the evidence is a scalar projection of the support-minus-complement margin onto one language direction; it is language-dependent but cannot express interactions that need more than one direction

verdict.reason: The standardized two-sample contrast repairs the trivial-partition degeneracy and reduces the null area bias without a free parameter. It still does not admit training: a fresh N1 re-check is required, the single language direction limitation remains, and no matched trained control exists yet.
